source_document.body:
GlobalFoundries broke ground Friday on a roughly $10 billion semiconductor plant in Malta, New York, the first of two factories planned under a U.S.-Japan investment agreement. The chipmaker expects the first plant to begin operating in 2029.
What’s Related
Once it reaches full production, the new plant is expected to produce about 900,000 wafers a year. Wafers are thin discs on which manufacturers build chips. GlobalFoundries said the facility will use 300-millimeter wafers, about 12 inches across, to make chips for vehicles, industrial equipment, and communications infrastructure .
Japan is providing up to $21 billion in funding for the two-plant plan, and New York State is providing $570 million in incentives to help move the first plant forward. GlobalFoundries was selected in October to provide the manufacturing technology and run both facilities.
400,000 wafers per year
The roughly 400,000-square-foot plant will go up at GlobalFoundries’ existing Malta campus, which serves as its global headquarters. The company says the site is already permitted for the project and can use existing infrastructure to speed construction.
The existing Malta facility has annual capacity for about 400,000 wafers on the same 300-millimeter basis, according to GlobalFoundries. The first new plant alone is designed to add more than twice that much capacity. Japanese chipmaker Renesas said in October that it is already factoring the additional New York capacity into its own production plans.
Who will own and run the plants?
GlobalFoundries told investors that an entity owned by the U.S. and Japanese governments would own the facilities and their manufacturing equipment. GlobalFoundries would build and run the plants, provide the chipmaking technology, and manage day-to-day costs such as labor , utilities, and materials. The government-owned entity would receive revenue from wafer sales.
Second plant still needs approval
The second Malta plant would receive a separate investment of about $10 billion and add room to make another 900,000 wafers a year. If approved and built, the two new facilities would together have annual capacity for about 1.8 million wafers at full production. GlobalFoundries gave a 2029 target for the first plant and has yet to announce a start date for the second.
GlobalFoundries estimates that the two-plant project would create more than 1,000 manufacturing jobs and about 27,000 jobs across construction and related businesses in New York’s Capital Region. The company says it is working with schools, colleges, and workforce development groups to train people for semiconductor manufacturing jobs.
